title: Finite-cover locality of bounded constructibility and a fixed Tor interval
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] whose underlying topological space is Noetherian, meaning that every descending chain of closed subsets stabilizes. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^r U_i$ be a finite open covering, with open immersions $j_i:U_i\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-open-immersion]; $r=0$ is allowed if $X$ is empty. Use the small pro-etale sites, constant coefficient ring sheaves, and derived categories of module sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and let $a\leq b$ be integers. Write $K_i=K|_{U_i}$ for derived restriction. Write $\mathcal H^t$ for cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Assume that for each $i$ only finitely many $\mathcal H^t(K_i)$ are nonzero, and each $\mathcal H^t(K_i)$ has a finite partition of $U_i$ into locally closed constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset] subschemes (with their reduced induced structure) on which its pullback is locally constant [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf] with finite $A$-module stalks. Assume also that for every degree-zero sheaf $F_i$ of $A$-modules on $(U_i)_{\mathrm{proet}}$ one has
$$\mathcal H^t(K_i\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}F_i)=0\quad(t\notin[a,b]),$$
using derived sheaf tensor [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Then each $\mathcal H^t(K)$ has a finite partition of $X$ into locally closed constructible subschemes on which it is locally constant with finite $A$-module stalks, and for every degree-zero sheaf $F$ of $A$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ one has
$$\mathcal H^t(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}F)=0\quad(t\notin[a,b]).$$
In particular $\mathcal H^t(K)=0$ for $t\notin[a,b]$, so $K$ is bounded constructible with Tor amplitude in that same interval.

proof.text: Every open subset of X is quasi-compact: otherwise a cover without a finite subcover yields, by successively adjoining a member containing an uncovered point, a strictly increasing chain of finite unions of covering opens, contrary to the descending-chain hypothesis on their closed complements. For the diagonal of X over Spec Z, the inverse image of any affine open is an open subset of X and hence quasi-compact. Thus X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, using the definition of quasi-separatedness. The affine-open basis now gives a finite affine refinement W_a of the given cover, with each W_a contained in some U_i. Intersect the local partitions with W_a. Their parts remain locally closed and constructible: their open and closed presentations restrict, and every open of a Noetherian space is quasi-compact, hence retrocompact. The same observation makes these parts constructible in X. No intersection of affine opens is asserted affine.

source.place: Tag 095F, lemma-constructible-local, and the affine refinement in lemma-constructible-quasi-compact-quasi-separated; affine basis Tag 01IT

proof.text:
For an open U in X, the localized site X_proet/U is U_proet: its objects are weakly etale maps V -> X factoring through U, equivalently weakly etale maps V -> U, with the same covering families. One direction follows by base change; the converse follows by composition with the open immersion. This is clause (1) and (4) of the weakly-etale localization lemma, whose clause (2) identifies the constant coefficient rings. The scheme-morphism inverse image along j_U is this localized restriction: the object inverse-image restriction lemma gives j_U^*G = G|_U naturally, for sheaves of sets, rings and A-modules, so pullbacks along open immersions in steps 3 and 4 are restrictions. Restriction j_U^* to this localized ringed site is exact. It therefore preserves kernels, images and quotients, giving j_U^* H^t(K) = H^t(K|_U) from the cohomology-sheaf formula. Apply the ringed-topos derived tensor pullback lemma to this localization, with R=A_X and S=R|_U. Exactness identifies Lj_U^* with termwise restriction and carries a degree-zero sheaf F to F|_U in degree zero. The lemma gives the natural comparison
$(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}F)|_U\simeq (K|_U)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(F|_U)$.
In particular this is valid for the original U_i and for their affine refinements. This uses the cited derived comparison, rather than inferring preservation of K-flatness from exactness alone.

proof.text: Fix a degree t. For each affine chart W_a use the partition obtained by intersecting its chosen U_i-partition for H^t(K_i) with W_a. The preceding cohomology identification identifies the restricted global sheaf H^t(K) with that local sheaf on W_a. Apply the finite affine stratification-local-gluing lemma: its quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypotheses hold by step 1. We obtain a finite constructible locally closed immersed stratification S of X and, for each stratum S_c, an actual factorization S_c -> T_a,d -> W_a -> X through one of these local strata. We may take the reduced induced structure on each S_c by precomposing its immersion and factorization with reduction; the image, local closedness, constructibility and partition are unchanged. The resulting reduced locally closed subscheme is the reduced induced one: locally its defining radical ideal is the radical of the ideal defining the original immersion. Consequently the pullback of H^t(K) to the reduced S_c is the pullback, along an actual scheme morphism, of the prescribed locally constant sheaf with finite stalks on a local stratum. Step 4 verifies exactly the two properties needed for that pullback. For the empty scheme the empty stratification already suffices.

proof.text: Here is the transport argument used in steps 1 and 3. For any scheme morphism h:Z -> T, base change carries a pro-etale family trivializing a locally constant sheaf L on T to a covering family on Z, by the covering-preserving base-change construction of pro-etale inverse image. Inverse image preserves constant sheaves: on underlying sets the constant sheaf with value M is the coproduct of M copies of the terminal sheaf; an inverse-image left adjoint preserves this coproduct and the terminal object. Applying inverse image to addition and scalar multiplication identifies this with the constant A-module sheaf with value M. The fixed-ring module inverse-image lemma supplies the coefficient-ring identification and its compatibility with localization. For a member T_j of the trivializing family put Z_j=Z x_T T_j. The localization lemma for ringed site morphisms, applied to u_h, V=T_j and U=u_h(T_j)=Z_j, with ring map c^h_A, gives (h^*L)|_{Z_j} = (h_{T_j})^*(L|_{T_j}) for the localized morphism h_{T_j}. Applying the constant-sheaf argument to h_{T_j} identifies this with the constant module sheaf with value M_j on the localized site. This proves local constancy by its definition. Finally the pro-etale inverse-image stalk lemma identifies each geometric stalk at z of h^*L with the stalk of L at h(z); forgetting module structure suffices to check finiteness. Thus finite stalks are retained. Apply this first to the open intersections of step 1 and then to the factorization morphisms of step 3.

proof.text: Let F be any degree-zero A-module sheaf on X and put F_i=F|_{U_i}. For t outside [a,b], the assumed local vanishing and step 2 identify the restriction of H^t(K tensor_A^L F) to every U_i with zero. The U_i form a covering family in X_proet: the open immersions are weakly etale, and for any affine V in X the intersections V intersect U_i admit affine refinements with a finite subcover of V, exactly the covering criterion in the site definition. Covering-family detection of vanishing, clause (1) of the pro-etale conservativity lemma, now gives H^t(K tensor_A^L F)=0. This applies to arbitrary F, not just locally constant coefficients, and the same fixed integers a,b are used on all members. It proves the asserted global Tor interval.

source.place: Tag 095F locality pattern; pro-etale covering-family detection as in the cited conservativity node

proof.text: Take F=A_X in step 5. In the K-flat definition of derived tensor, a representative P of K satisfies P tensor_A A_X = P termwise, with the same differentials; hence K tensor_A^L A_X is K. Thus H^t(K)=0 outside the finite integer interval [a,b]. For each remaining degree, steps 1--4 give its finite partition with locally constant finite stalks. This is the claimed bounded constructibility. The given local boundedness is consistent with, but not needed in addition to, the stronger common Tor bound. If X is empty, the empty covering detection criterion yields the zero sheaf and all conclusions still hold.
